name: Delphinus
introduction: is the Dolphin, a small but charming constellation that really looks like a leaping dolphin. In Greek myth, a dolphin persuaded the sea nymph Amphitrite to marry Poseidon, or rescued the poet Arion from pirates. Its diamond of four stars is known as Job’s Coffin. It is best seen on northern summer and autumn evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Delphinus hides a joke in its star names. [Sualocin](hip:101958) and [Rotanev](hip:101769) look like Arabic names, but read backward they spell Nicolaus Venator, the Latinized name of Niccolò Cacciatore, an assistant at the Palermo Observatory, who slipped them into a star catalog in 1814.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Rotanev](hip:101769), the brightest star, is a binary whose two stars orbit each other every 27 years. [Gamma² Delphini](hip:102532) is a lovely golden and greenish double in a small telescope. [Aldulfin](hip:101421) marks the dolphin’s tail.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: In 2013, Nova Delphini briefly became visible to the naked eye. The distant globular clusters NGC 6934 and NGC 7006 also lie in Delphinus, the latter far out in the Milky Way’s halo.
